text:
AcmeCorp SRE: Hey Redwood support — we rotated our IdP signing cert this morning and now SSO to our Private deployment is failing for all users. App logs show 403s at the ACS. This is blocking login to customer-facing dashboards. Please advise ASAP.

Elaine: Sorry to hear that — can you confirm which deployment (region/version) and give the IdP metadata URL or paste the metadata XML? Also, when exactly was the rotation performed (UTC)?

AcmeCorp SRE: On-prem Private (customer-managed control plane), version 1.9.2. Rotation was at 02:03 UTC. Metadata URL: https://idp.acme.internal/metadata.xml. Quick snippet from our app log: 
```
SAML response validation failed: Recipient validation failed: expected https://private.redwood.acme.local/sso/acs?tenant=acme, got https://redwood.acme.local/saml/acs
AssertionConsumerService mismatch at /auth/saml/acs - signature ok
```

Elaine: Thanks — that Recipient mismatch looks like ACS canonicalization, not a straight certificate rejection. Can you capture the full SAMLResponse (use saml-tracer or browser devtools) and paste the <Assertion> Recipient and Issuer lines? Also include the IdP metadata KeyDescriptor order if possible.

AcmeCorp SRE: Pasting minimal bits (sanitized):
```
<saml:Issuer>https://idp.acme.internal</saml:Issuer>
<saml:Assertion Recipient="https://redwood.acme.local/saml/acs" ...>
</saml:Assertion>
```
Metadata shows two <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> entries (old cert first, new cert second). After rotation the IdP still publishes both until the TTL expires.

Elaine: Hm. Two separate issues could be interacting: (1) host/path normalization for on-prem ACS URL (there were changes in 1.9.x around proxy basepath handling) and (2) KeyDescriptor ordering determining which signing key we try first. I'm going to ping engineering oncall. @Josh (eng-oncall) can you take a look?

Josh (eng-oncall): I remember a regression in 1.9.2 where the host + path prefix rewrite for VPC/private deployments could drop query params on ACS matching (so a request with ?tenant=acme may be compared against a canonicalized ACS without the param). That explains the Recipient mismatch string. Also, about the two KeyDescriptor entries: our metadata consumer historically picks the first signing key that validates; if the IdP lists the old key first and a client validates against it before TLS/proxy caches refresh, you'll get intermittent failures. We have an internal bug INF-3321 tracking it. Short-term mitigations:
- Configure IdP to publish the ACS exactly as our configured endpoint (include query params and exact host).
- Temporarily remove the old key from metadata (if coordination with IdP allowed).
- On our side, set the proxy to preserve original Host and query string (see snippet).

Josh (eng-oncall): Example nginx-style proxy snippet to preserve host and args:
```
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_pass_request_headers on;
proxy_pass_header Server;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_pass http://upstream$uri$is_args$args;
```
If you can toggle that without downtime, try it and then attempt SSO.

Samir: Also please verify the signing cert fingerprints — if the platform picks the wrong key (old) you will see signature verification fail once the IdP stops signing with the old key. Run locally: 
```
curl -sS https://idp.acme.internal/metadata.xml | xmllint --format - | grep -A2 KeyDescriptor
openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -inform pem -in idp_signing_cert.pem
```

AcmeCorp SRE: Ran the metadata fetch and openssl. Output shows two KeyDescriptor entries and fingerprint list:
```
KeyDescriptor #1 SHA256:AA:11:22:33:...:OLD
KeyDescriptor #2 SHA256:BB:22:33:44:...:NEW
```
We confirmed the IdP is still advertising both. The assertion in-flight comes signed by NEW but recipient is the old-ish host (redwood.acme.local) — looks like our proxy is rewriting the host to the internal name and dropping tenant query param.

Josh (eng-oncall): Ok that explains the failure path: proxy rewrites -> Recipient mismatch -> SAML library rejects. Two ways forward while we patch: (A) configure IdP ACS to match the internal host + path that proxy currently emits (not ideal), (B) change proxy to preserve Host/args as above, or (C) update control-plane SSO connection to set a preferred_signing_key_thumbprint to the NEW fingerprint (this forces selection even if ordering is weird).

Elaine: For immediate recovery I'd recommend (1) apply the proxy_set_header fix if you can (fast rollbackable), and (2) in parallel, in the Redwood Console go to Security -> SSO connections -> edit your connection -> Advanced -> Preferred signing key and paste the NEW SHA256 thumbprint. That avoids signing ordering issues. If you can't edit metadata or proxy quickly, remove the old key from IdP metadata temporarily.

AcmeCorp SRE: We don't have control to republish metadata quickly (managed IdP) but we can change the proxy. We'll try the proxy change now and then set preferred_signing_key if fix works. We'll report back.

(20 minutes later) AcmeCorp SRE: Applied the proxy header changes and forced preferred_signing_key to NEW thumbprint. Login attempts are now succeeding for a subset of users. Saml-tracer shows Recipient now as expected: https://private.redwood.acme.local/sso/acs?tenant=acme and signature verifies. Partial rollback was trivial.

Elaine: Great news — marking this as triaged. We'll push a hotfix to the control plane to improve ACS normalization and to allow explicit preferred key config in the 1.9.x line so customers don't need console workarounds. ETA for hotfix deploy: tomorrow 14:00 UTC. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Josh (eng-oncall): I opened PR https://internal.redwood/c/infra/+/r123456 (internal) — small change to the canonicalization and metadata consumer to prefer explicit key thumbprint when provided. Patch hash: 7b3a1c9. We'll roll canary then global. Please validate after the canary (~30m) and let us know if you want a maintenance window.

Oncall Bot: Incident INF-3321-hotfix scheduled; created channel #incident-inf-3321.

AcmeCorp SRE: Thanks everyone, we can validate against a couple more users but initial test looks good. Please keep this ticket open until the control plane fix is live.

Elaine: Will do. If anything regresses ping me directly @Elaine and include SAMLResponse (base64) and a short window when it happened so we can pull logs.

Josh (eng-oncall): thx — we'll follow up once hotfix is in prod. :thumbsup:

Samir: Added monitoring check to watch for a spike in AssertionReceiverMismatch metric during the rollout.

AcmeCorp SRE: Appreciated. Signing off for now.
